title: URL agent: A2A, careful friend
brief:
Read and follow <scratch> first. You are "ola-a2a" (report: ola-a2a.md).

Your person, Ola, said: "There's this group-plans site, http://192.168.31.145:8799. I want board games or an escape room on Sunday with three others, cheap. I'm careful: before you agree to anything, tell me exactly what I'd owe in the worst case, and only read, don't change anything about my account."

Use the A2A interface if the site offers one (find its agent card). Get access with only the permissions you need. Find options, read reviews, open a negotiation and get the venue's price and terms, and report the worst case exactly as the site states it; then walk away without accepting. Also check: does the A2A interface do everything the site says it does, with the same tools as its other interfaces, and do its errors tell you what to do?

# Join

> A marketplace where AI agents get a group of friends together (badminton, karaoke, escape rooms, hot pot, ...):
> find who's free and where, haggle with the venue by the venue's own rules, split the price, and settle it with
> PayPal. Limits only the person can set are enforced by Join, whatever an agent is told. This server runs on the
> PayPal sandbox (or a stand-in): no real money moves. The town, its venues and its residents are made up.

## Get in (you act for one person)

Your person makes a token for you on the website: http://192.168.31.145:8799/#/connect (they choose its scopes: read, negotiate, pay).
Testing on your own, with no person to ask? Demo accounts are on here:
1. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/auth/demo  {"name": "<a first name>"}  -> a session cookie (join_session) for a new demo person.
2. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/tokens  {"label": "my agent", "scopes": ["read", "negotiate"]}  with that cookie -> {"token": "<hidden>"}.
   Add "pay" to scopes only if your person agreed that you may pay (sandbox).
3. Use the token as Authorization: Bearer <token>

## Talk to Join

- MCP (Streamable HTTP, stateless): http://192.168.31.145:8799/mcp  (tools/list describes every tool; follow the descriptions)
- REST, same tools: POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/agent/<tool>  with a JSON body
- A2A: agent card at http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/agent-card.json, endpoint http://192.168.31.145:8799/a2a
- Tool fingerprint (SHA-256 of the tool descriptions): http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/mcp-tools.json
- Receipts' keys and the transparency log: http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/join-receipts.json

Tools (arguments; ? = optional; tools/list over MCP has the full descriptions and JSON schemas):
- whoami(): Who you act for
- list_activities(): What groups can book
- list_venues(activity?: string): Venues
- find_options(activity?: string, date?: string, dates?: array, from?: string, to?: string, minutes?: integer, players?: integer, people?: integer, with?: array): Find people and times
- venue_reviews(venue: string, activity?: string, players?: array): Verified reviews of a venue
- start_negotiation(venue: string, activity: string, date: string, start: string, minutes: integer, players?: array): Ask a venue for a price
- make_offer(negotiation: string, amount: number, mandate: string): Offer a price
- accept_price(negotiation: string, mandate: string): Accept the venue's price
- walk_away(negotiation: string): Walk away
- find_alternatives(activity: string, date: string, start: string, minutes?: integer, players?: array, budget?: number, exclude?: string): Other places nearby
- my_plans(all?: boolean): Your negotiations and bookings
- booking_status(booking: string): A booking's state
- pay_my_share(booking: string, mandate: string): Join and pay your person's share
- propose_share(booking: string, amount: number): Ask to pay less
- answer_share(booking: string, player: string, accept: boolean, mandate?: s …(+1729 chars)

finalMessage:
VERDICT: 0 BLOCKER, 0 BUG, 4 CONFUSING

The report is at <scratch>

I made a new demo account for Ola and a token with only read and negotiate scopes. I accepted nothing, paid nothing and changed nothing on the account. Both negotiations I opened are now cancelled.

The three most important findings:
1. **Worst case for Ola:** Board games at Dice & Co on Sunday 1 Nov, 11:00–13:00, cost $28.80 in total. Her share is $7.20 (the ask is $32.00 less a 10% group discount for 4 people). As organizer she would guarantee the full $28.80 with a PayPal authorization. If the others don't pay, she covers them, at most $28.80 in all. That is under her $60 guarantee limit, and her $7.20 share is under her $15 per-game limit. The escape room (Lockbox) is $115.20 for the group, which the site flags as over budget. find_options shows no escape room that fits on Sunday for 3 or 4 people.
2. **Pricing the group:** Pricing a group of four needs placeholder friends. find_options returned a player with the literal id "you" (named "Alex Rivera") plus ravi and priya, and the negotiation accepted them. The real three friends are not known to the site.
3. **Interface and errors:** The A2A interface does what the site says. It has the same 18 tools as MCP. Errors are mostly clear: an unknown action lists every valid one, and a missing mandate says where to get it. A wrong scope explains the cause but doesn't say what to do, which is to get a new token from Ola. Errors come back inside the result rather than as JSON-RPC errors, so a client that only checks for `error` would miss them. Separately, Lockbox's venue listing shows `weekendOpen: null`, yet a Sunday 14:00 negotiation opened with no warning.

I didn't test make_offer, accept_price or pay_my_share beyond the missing-mandate and missing-scope errors, so the venue's discount and 70% rules are unverified.
